properties.name: Glyphosate-resistant creeping bentgrass — spread into wild Agrostis
properties.type: Grass, transgene escape into wild relatives
properties.size: Established in wild populations across multiple counties
properties.desc: Creeping bentgrass engineered to survive glyphosate, grown in trials for the golf-course market, moved out of its plots into resident populations and hybridised with wild relatives. It is the strongest documented case of transgene spread into wild plant communities anywhere, it was found by accident during unrelated fieldwork, and the plants are still there — eradication was attempted for years and abandoned.

properties.name: GloFish — fluorescent transgenic fish established in Brazilian streams
properties.type: Ornamental fish, escape into wild waters
properties.size: Multiple streams in the Atlantic Forest region
properties.desc: Fluorescent transgenic zebrafish, sold as aquarium pets since 2003, spread from ornamental fish farms and established breeding populations in Atlantic Forest streams. The pathway was never the aquarium. It was the farm supplying them, and nobody was monitoring it because a decorative pet was not treated as an environmental question.

properties.name: StarLink maize — unapproved variety in the human food supply
properties.type: Maize, unapproved variety in food
properties.size: Estimated 300+ recalled food products
properties.desc: A maize approved only for animal feed turned up in taco shells and hundreds of other foods, triggering a nationwide recall in 2000. It had entered the human supply through ordinary grain handling, and the episode is why segregating an approved-for-feed-only crop is now generally treated as impossible in practice.

properties.name: LLRICE 601 — unapproved rice in the US commercial supply
properties.type: Rice, unapproved variety in commerce
properties.state: Arkansas and the US rice belt
properties.size: US rice exports; EU and Japan import suspensions
properties.desc: An experimental rice line never approved for sale was found throughout the US commercial supply, having spread from research plots years earlier. Exports were rejected, prices collapsed, and farmers who had never planted it carried the loss.

properties.name: Triffid flax — deregistered line found in exports a decade later
properties.type: Flax, deregistered variety in exports
properties.size: Canadian flax exports to the EU
properties.desc: A flax variety deregistered in Canada in 2001 to protect European exports appeared in European shipments a decade later. Deregistration removed the paperwork; it did not remove the seed, which persisted in the system long after the record said it was gone.

properties.name: Transgenes in Mexican maize landraces
properties.type: Maize, transgene presence in landraces
properties.size: Multiple communities across several states
properties.desc: Engineered sequences found in maize landraces in Oaxaca, the crop's centre of origin. This is not cross-breeding into a crop but into the reservoir every commercial maize variety on Earth was ultimately bred from, and Mexico has had to defend its restrictions against a US trade challenge since.

properties.name: Feral herbicide-tolerant canola with stacked traits, roadsides
properties.type: Canola, feral populations with stacked traits
properties.size: Roadside populations across the state
properties.desc: Canola growing wild along North Dakota roadsides, carrying herbicide-tolerance traits — and some plants carrying traits from two different companies, a combination nobody bred, made by plants breeding with each other outside any field.

properties.name: Jacobina — engineered mosquito genome entering the wild population
properties.type: Mosquito, introgression from release strain
properties.size: 27 months of weekly releases, ~450,000 males per week
properties.desc: Researchers found the engineered mosquito lineage released at Jacobina had introgressed into the local wild population, which the company had said would not happen. The finding came from independent scientists rather than from any monitoring attached to the release.

properties.name: Bt10 maize — wrong unapproved line shipped for four years
properties.type: Maize, unapproved line distributed in error
properties.state: United States (exports to EU and Japan)
properties.size: Estimated tens of thousands of tonnes
properties.desc: An unapproved maize line was shipped to Europe and Japan for four years because the company had confused it with an approved one. Nobody noticed until testing at the destination, which means the error was in the identity of the material rather than in its containment.

properties.name: Unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton planted at scale
properties.type: Cotton, unapproved trait planted commercially
properties.size: Estimated millions of hectares
properties.desc: Unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton was found planted across large areas of India before any approval process had assessed it. The seed moved through informal channels ahead of the regulator, which is a sequence several countries have followed.

properties.name: Bt63 rice — unapproved GM rice in food products and exports
properties.type: Rice, unapproved variety in food chain
properties.size: Detected in exports to Europe over many years
properties.desc: Unapproved GM rice was found in food products and exports from China, traced to research material that had reached farmers. Rice is a staple eaten directly, which makes the food-safety argument here less abstract than for feed crops.

properties.name: GM petunias — engineered ornamentals found in worldwide commerce
properties.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety in trade
properties.size: Dozens of varieties across many countries
properties.desc: Petunias sold worldwide as ornamentals were found to be engineered, decades after research lines had apparently entered the trade. Nobody had been checking flowers, because ornamentals were not thought of as organisms anyone needed to track.

properties.name: Roundup Ready wheat — unapproved wheat in an Oregon field
properties.type: Wheat, unapproved line found volunteering
properties.size: Export suspensions by Japan and South Korea
properties.desc: Wheat engineered to survive glyphosate, never approved anywhere, found growing in an Oregon field years after the trials ended. Japan and South Korea suspended US wheat imports. No route from the trial plots to that field was ever established.

properties.name: GM papaya — unapproved virus-resistant plants in commercial orchards
properties.type: Papaya, unapproved variety in cultivation
properties.size: Orchards across multiple provinces
properties.desc: Unapproved virus-resistant papaya was found in commercial plantings in Thailand, having spread from a research station. Papaya is propagated and traded locally, so material moves through channels no register follows.

properties.name: Herbicide-tolerant bentgrass — second spread via seed movement
properties.type: Grass, secondary spread beyond control area
properties.state: Malheur County, Oregon and into Idaho
properties.status: Spread beyond the designated control area
properties.size: Irrigation canals and adjacent land in two states
properties.desc: A second bentgrass spread, this time through seed movement rather than pollen, into a different watershed. The first incident had prompted monitoring; the second showed the monitoring was watching the wrong pathway.

properties.name: Bt cotton found growing before any approval existed
properties.type: Cotton, unapproved trait in commercial fields
properties.size: Estimated tens of thousands of hectares before approval
properties.desc: Bt cotton was found growing in Gujarat before India had approved any engineered crop, and the government had to decide retroactively what to do with a harvest already in the market. It chose to approve.

properties.name: GM oilseed rape naturalised around import ports
properties.type: Canola, feral populations at import points
properties.size: Roadsides between ports and crushing plants
properties.desc: Engineered oilseed rape found naturalised around Japanese ports and along the roads inland from them, spilled from imported grain in transit. Japan grows none of it. The plants arrived as cargo.

properties.name: Engineered petunias — second wave found after the first recall
properties.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety in trade
properties.size: Further varieties on sale years after the first clearance
properties.desc: A second wave of engineered petunias found in the United States and Europe after the first recall, showing the material had never been fully removed from the ornamental trade.

properties.name: Herbicide-tolerant canola in a country that never approved it
properties.type: Canola, unapproved trait in cultivation
properties.size: Certified seed lots and adjacent crops
properties.desc: Herbicide-tolerant canola found growing in New South Wales, in a state that had not approved it. Seed moves along roads with the trucks carrying it.

properties.name: Engineered wheat found again, years after the first Oregon case
properties.type: Wheat, unapproved line found volunteering
properties.size: Isolated fields; export markets disrupted again
properties.desc: Engineered wheat found again in Washington and Montana, years after the Oregon incident and in different states. Two unexplained appearances of a crop never commercialised anywhere.

properties.name: Farmed salmon genetics established in wild Norwegian rivers
properties.type: Salmon, genetic introgression into wild populations
properties.status: Documented in a majority of assessed rivers
properties.size: Assessed across ~200 wild populations
properties.desc: Norwegian monitoring finds farmed salmon genetics in a large majority of assessed wild rivers. Nothing engineered is involved: intensive selection plus escapes from pens has already changed wild fish, which is the baseline any argument about engineered salmon starts from.

properties.name: Atlantic salmon established in Patagonian rivers after farm spread
properties.type: Salmon, introduced species established after spread
properties.size: Multiple river systems; single spread of hundreds of thousands of fish
properties.desc: Atlantic salmon, not native to Chile, have spread out of farms in very large numbers and established in Patagonian rivers. Again nothing engineered — just farming at scale in a place the species could survive.

properties.name: Engineered petunias in a third wave, years after two recalls
properties.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety recurring in trade
properties.state: European and North American horticultural trade
properties.size: Varieties still surfacing after two clearance rounds
properties.desc: A third wave of engineered petunias, years after two recalls. Each round was described as the end of it.

properties.name: Unapproved GM soy planted across Ukraine
properties.type: Soy, unapproved trait in commercial cultivation
properties.size: Estimated a substantial share of the national soy crop
properties.desc: Unapproved GM soy planted across a large share of Ukrainian soy area, in a country with no functioning approval system. A country with no register does not thereby have no engineered crops; it has no record of them.

properties.name: GM maize found growing in Mexico despite the planting prohibition
properties.type: Maize, unapproved cultivation in a centre of origin
properties.size: Detected in commercial fields and in tortilla samples
properties.desc: GM maize found growing in Mexico despite the planting prohibition, in the north where seed crosses the border with trade. A prohibition on planting does not stop seed arriving.

properties.name: Paraíba do Sul basin — recorded spread
properties.type: Recorded spread
properties.state: Muriaé, Minas Gerais — headwater creeks of the Paraíba do Sul basin, Atlantic Forest
properties.desc: The first engineered animal known to have established a self-sustaining population in the wild. Fluorescent zebrafish were found in all five sampled headwater creeks of the southeastern Paraíba do Sul basin, first seen in 2015, beside Latin America's largest ornamental aquaculture centre whose roughly 4,500 ponds discharge into those streams. Surveys since show them breeding year-round with a peak in the rainy season, and reaching maturity earlier than unmodified zebrafish, which speeds the cycle further. They are banned in Brazil and were still being advertised for sale there. A single specimen found in Florida canals in 2014 did not establish, most likely because something ate it; here there is no predator that takes them. Three things line up in one record: a ban that did not stop the sale, a pond wall that was the entire containment measure, and a trait that is visible to the naked eye — which is the only reason anyone noticed at all.
